cut fetches the target branch from origin and prepares the release from its
tip in a scratch checkout: it resolves the base version and the signal floor,
authors the changelog from the commits' evidence, suggests the bump, has it
confirmed, writes the rendered section into CHANGELOG.md, runs
commands.propagate to write the version into the manifests (with
RELEASE_VERSION set), refuses a change to any path that is neither
CHANGELOG.md nor in release_paths, and runs commands.validate. Only then
does it write: it creates the stage branch at the fetched tip, commits the
release as "Release <version>" with a Release-Type trailer carrying the
confirmed bump, pushes the branch to origin, and opens a pull request into
the target with gh. Your working tree, index and current branch are never
read or changed.

bump is major, minor or patch, and is a decision that needs no confirmation;
below the suggestion it proceeds with a warning, and below the signal floor
or over a range with nothing releasable it is refused unless --force is
given. Without a bump the suggested bump must be confirmed: --yes accepts
it; on a terminal cut shows it with its reasons and asks; otherwise cut
halts, answering the suggestion, and exits 1. On a terminal cut also shows
the writes it will make and asks once before the first, unless --yes. It
never tags, publishes, merges, or changes the target branch. Exits 1 when it
refuses or halts, having written nothing, and 3 when a write failed after
another succeeded, having reported every write it made. If the push fails,
cut deletes the local stage branch it created.

Usage:
  release cut [bump] [flags]

Flags:
      --dry-run           Report every intended action and the changelog section, and change nothing
      --force             Stage the named bump even when it is below the signal floor or the range holds nothing releasable. Requires bump
  -h, --help              help for cut
      --json              Render the answer as JSON instead of YAML
      --no-pull-request   Create and push the stage branch and stop; open no pull request
      --redo-notes        Discard any cached corpus and author again
      --skip-notes        Author with the mechanical producer in place of an authoring exchange
      --target branch     The release line to cut from: a branch on origin (default: the configured target, else the branch origin/HEAD points to)
      --yes               Do not prompt: accept the suggested bump when none is named, and proceed to the writes

Global Flags:
      --config file   Use this configuration file instead of discovering one
  -C, --repo path     Operate on the repository at this path instead of the working directory
